roles.title: MiLB strength & conditioning coordinator
roles.sourceStatus: Generic role archetype built from public job-posting patterns. Not a specific posting.
roles.scopeNotes: Coordinator pathway: coaching quality, staff development, standards, and operations across affiliates. This map does not assess applicant eligibility.
duties: Manage and mentor affiliate, FCL, and Dominican Republic coaches; conduct staff evaluations.
Oversee budgets, facilities, and equipment operations.
Deliver science-led programming and testing/rehabilitation protocols.
Coach sprinting, deceleration, multidirectional movement, and safe exercise technique.
Collaborate across disciplines, communicate player goals and reports, and continue professional education.

roles.title: Minor league S&C coordinator
roles.sourceStatus: Generic role archetype built from public job-posting patterns. Not a specific posting.
roles.scopeNotes: Coordinator pathway: staffing, affiliate support, monitoring, and interdisciplinary communication. The saved application label is retained; the exact employer title needs the original posting.
duties: Oversee and develop minor league coaches, plan annual staffing, and support affiliate implementation.
Coordinate with medical, baseball science, and nutrition staff.
Manage monitoring, player communication, and off-season remote check-ins.
Maintain equipment standards and evaluate the department.

roles.title: Minor league S&C coach (affiliate)
roles.sourceStatus: Generic role archetype built from public job-posting patterns. Not a specific posting.
roles.scopeNotes: Affiliate pathway: daily implementation, scheduling, testing, and player communication. Employer screening expectations do not establish that a screen predicts injury.
duties: Implement organizational protocols during spring training, the Triple A season, and off-season camps.
Design strength, power, conditioning, and individualized position-specific development programs.
Conduct testing with sports medicine/performance science and use objective metrics for programming and development.
Integrate game/training loads, recovery, and training modifications into practice and competitive schedules with affiliate staff.
Use movement screening and biomechanical analysis when applicable; report player progress, program effectiveness, and affiliate operations.
Assist return-to-play and sports medicine with immediate injury support, first aid, stabilization, and crisis protocols.

roles.title: Minor league S&C coach
roles.sourceStatus: Generic role archetype built from public job-posting patterns. Not a specific posting.
roles.scopeNotes: Affiliate pathway: daily coaching, testing records, and reports under travel and seasonal demands. Use only the duties preserved in the saved summary.
duties: Provide daily coaching and program implementation.
Conduct objective testing and maintain participation/workload records.
Provide weekly/monthly reports to S&C leadership.
Work within spring training, seasonal affiliate relocation, and US/DR travel demands.

roles.title: Associate major league S&C coach
roles.sourceStatus: Generic role archetype built from public job-posting patterns. Not a specific posting.
roles.scopeNotes: Major League support pathway: assist daily S&C delivery within the department, communicate observations, and follow assigned responsibilities.
duties: Support individualized objective-assessment and position-informed programs under MLB S&C leadership.
Assist position-specific energy-system programs; coach movement preparation, linear/multidirectional skills, speed, plyometrics, strength, power, corrective exercise, and recovery under direction.
Carry out established readiness/workload protocols; assist testing and record subjective/objective information accurately.
Maintain athlete-management records and information transfers between Major and Minor Leagues.
Prepare weekly updates and support midyear/end-of-year testing reports.
Seek feedback, develop expertise, and collaborate with medical/rehab, science, nutrition, and baseball staff while building professional relationships.

roles.title: Applied performance scientist
roles.sourceStatus: Generic role archetype built from public job-posting patterns. Not a specific posting.
roles.scopeNotes: Applied science pathway: collect and interpret data, maintain reproducible workflows, and communicate results in baseball context. Analysis does not itself establish causality or clinical authority.
duties: Lead standardized workload monitoring and its interpretation, education, and application across performance, medical, and coaching groups.
Integrate physical, mechanical, workload, and performance information into shared processes.
Monitor workload trends and communicate concerns; support playing-time projections and physical capacity/game-demand comparison.
Profile players and benchmark against position/level-specific norms for evaluation and development.
Support injury-risk modeling and applied research on availability and on-field performance; evaluate emerging practice.
Conduct ad-hoc analyses and reports; improve workflows and communication using data, technology, and people.

roles.title: Medical & rehabilitation coordinator
roles.sourceStatus: Generic role archetype built from public job-posting patterns. Not a specific posting.
roles.scopeNotes: Clinical leadership pathway: medical coordination and rehabilitation require the professional credentials, experience, and clinical authority specified by the employer. Completing the hub does not provide those qualifications.
duties: Lead DR academy medical operations, treatment schedules, coverage, and in-scope direct care; document routine decisions and escalate complex/high-risk cases.
Coordinate priority/complex postsurgical cases and individualized rehab using objective tests, loading, baseball milestones, organization criteria, and physician guidance.
Communicate readiness, restrictions, and unresolved concerns before participation changes; clearance follows designated physicians and organization protocols.
Develop staff through feedback/case review, delegate within competence, and support early concern reporting and professional boundaries.
Coordinate interdisciplinary updates, preferred-language care education, provider networks, diagnostics, and rehearsed emergency action plans.
Manage onboarding and care transitions with receiving clinicians, records, restrictions, and follow-up; maintain accurate approved EMR documentation and authorized sharing.
Review injury/rehab outcomes and care delays; manage resources, coverage, credentials, continuing education, and mentorship.

roles.title: Rehab & academy S&C manager
roles.sourceStatus: Generic role archetype built from public job-posting patterns. Not a specific posting.
roles.scopeNotes: Rehab and academy pathway: integrate physical preparation with clinical care, player development, and return to baseball. Medical clearance remains with the responsible clinical team.
duties: Lead physical preparation during rehabilitation from early loading through return to full baseball participation.
Collaborate with medical/performance staff on objective rehabilitation plans, progressions, and return-to-performance criteria.
Coach individualized strength, power, speed, and energy-system programs based on injury considerations, player needs, and baseball demands.
Use performance data in rehab decisions, address physical qualities affected by time loss or considered relevant to risk, and prepare a deliberate transition to team demands.
Communicate status, progress, limitations, and next steps to stakeholders.
Lead academy S&C technical operations, support program design and problem solving, and maintain coaching/testing/monitoring standards with appropriate coach autonomy.
Develop coaches through observation, feedback, education, mentorship, onboarding, and communication with leadership.

competencies.title: Baseball role and demand analysis
competencies.description: Translate position, level, schedule, travel, training history, and player goals into physical-development priorities. This is a curriculum interpretation of individualized programming and profiling duties.
competencies.assessment: Produce a one-page needs analysis for a starter, reliever, and position player; distinguish measured demands, assumptions, missing information, and two priority decisions.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Baseball-specific time-motion/exposure research with population and competition level; organizational practice demands; contextual player interviews and authorized records.

competencies.title: Strength, power, and rotational preparation
competencies.description: Connect force capacity, movement skill, and rapid force expression to individualized baseball training without equating a gym test with batting or throwing performance.
competencies.assessment: Design and justify a four-week strength/power block with exercise intent, dose, progression/regression, and two monitoring decisions; explain limits of transfer claims.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Resistance-training and power-development evidence, baseball transfer studies, reliable test protocols, and athlete-specific constraints. Separate experimental evidence from practitioner examples.

competencies.title: Sprint, deceleration, and multidirectional coaching
competencies.description: Teach acceleration, exposure to speed, braking, and directional changes while accounting for position and recent exposure.
competencies.assessment: Annotate a simulated field session with cues, distances, recovery, progression, surface constraints, and stop/escalation decisions; include a base-running or fielding case.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Sprint/deceleration research, baseball running demands, and coaching observation. Label cross-sport findings and avoid unvalidated universal injury-prevention claims.

competencies.title: Position-specific energy-system development
competencies.description: Match conditioning to playing role, repeat-effort demands, and training recovery; distinguish aerobic support from game-specific activity.
competencies.assessment: Compare conditioning plans for a starter and an everyday outfielder; specify work/rest and expected adaptations, then revise for a congested week.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Baseball demand studies, conditioning adaptation research, and individualized tolerance/recovery information; hypothetical session doses must be explicitly labeled.

competencies.title: Annual planning and adaptable microcycles
competencies.description: Coordinate development, competitive preparation, travel, and uncertain opportunities across the baseball calendar.
competencies.assessment: Build linked off-season, spring-training, and in-season examples; adapt a starter microcycle to a rainout and a reliever plan to an unexpected appearance without inferring readiness from pitch count alone.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Periodization and dose-maintenance evidence, baseball schedules, complete practice/throwing/training records, and staff-defined priorities. Separate planning examples from tested prescriptions.

competencies.title: Session delivery and safe exercise coaching
competencies.description: Convert a written plan into clear coaching, observation, feedback, sensible progressions, and an organized training environment.
competencies.assessment: Teach back one strength and one movement session using a structured observation checklist; justify a regression and document a concern requiring referral.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Exercise instruction resources, supervised practical coaching, equipment procedures, and direct feedback. A quiz cannot demonstrate hands-on coaching competence.

competencies.title: Standardized testing and device protocols
competencies.description: Select feasible tests, standardize collection, and preserve protocol/device metadata so repeated results remain interpretable.
competencies.assessment: Write and execute a simulated SOP for a jump, sprint, and strength test: warm-up, trials, rest, device setup, units, invalid-trial rules, and documentation.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Validity/reliability studies for the exact population, protocol and device; manufacturer instructions for operation; local repeatability work before consequential use.

competencies.title: Measurement error and defensible interpretation
competencies.description: Interpret change and profiling with reliability, uncertainty, reference populations, and practical relevance.
competencies.assessment: Analyze a small repeated-test dataset; calculate a suitable error estimate, distinguish typical error/SEM from a change threshold, and explain why a changed score may not change the plan.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Measurement-theory sources and protocol-specific reliability data; justified benchmarking samples; documented calculations and limitations rather than universal cutoffs.

competencies.title: Workload records and contextual decisions
competencies.description: Maintain complete exposure records and combine training, throwing, game, recovery, and clinical context without turning one metric into clearance.
competencies.assessment: Audit a fictional week with missing bullpen/warm-up throws and missing session records; separate unknown from zero, identify questions, and produce a conditional recommendation with responsible decision owner.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Monitoring research and organizational recording definitions; complete internal/external load context. No ACWR “safe zone,” automated clearance, or availability inference from game counts.

competencies.title: Reproducible analysis and data workflows
competencies.description: Use appropriate SQL, R, or Python workflows to join, check, analyze, and document performance data. Tool depth is principally a science-role recommendation.
competencies.assessment: Create a reproducible synthetic-data report with data dictionary, join checks, missingness flags, units, versioned code, and a one-command rebuild; explain one failed quality check.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Approved schema/export specifications, reproducible-analysis standards, data-quality examples, and documented transformation tests. Use synthetic or properly de-identified data for study.

competencies.title: Reports that support a named decision
competencies.description: Communicate what changed, what is uncertain, which action is proposed, who owns it, and when to reassess.
competencies.assessment: Write a weekly affiliate update and a 60-second staff briefing from the same fictional case; include evidence, restrictions, alternatives, and a next review date.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Preserved reporting duties plus examples approved for teaching; stakeholder feedback on clarity/usefulness. Do not invent outcome effects or imply model certainty.

competencies.title: Research appraisal and model limitations
competencies.description: Evaluate intervention claims, injury-risk associations, and models before applying them to an individual baseball player.
competencies.assessment: Critique one baseball study and one cross-sport study using design, population, effect uncertainty, confounding, and applicability; audit a hypothetical risk model for leakage, calibration, validation, and harmful decisions.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Accessible primary research, reporting/validation guidance, and transparent model documentation; prospective/out-of-sample validation before operational claims. Employer aspirations are not scientific validation.

competencies.title: Functional anatomy and injury mechanisms
competencies.description: Explain shoulder, elbow, and hamstring anatomy and plausible baseball loading mechanisms. These regional priorities are curriculum choices, not a claim that every posting specifies these injuries.
competencies.assessment: Identify structures and actions in an anatomy model, explain a mechanism with uncertainty, and distinguish an educational hypothesis from a diagnosis; acknowledge missing/approximate model structures.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Authoritative anatomy references; verified 3D structure and attachment provenance; clinical/mechanical research. No invented ligament meshes or unverified attachment footprints.

competencies.title: Rehabilitation loading within assigned scope
competencies.description: Understand how medical restrictions, procedure-specific considerations, symptoms, tissue capacity, and response guide physical preparation alongside the clinical plan.
competencies.assessment: For a simulated operative and nonoperative case, identify missing clinical information, draft a conditional physical-preparation progression, and specify when to hold/refer and who must authorize changes.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Diagnosis/procedure-specific accessible rehabilitation evidence; physician/surgical restrictions and authorized clinician guidance for real cases. Time elapsed alone is insufficient; educational work confers no clinical authority.

competencies.title: Return to baseball performance
competencies.description: Distinguish participation, sport, and performance; integrate physical capacity, baseball tasks, exposure progression, confidence, and ongoing monitoring under team criteria.
competencies.assessment: Create a simulated return-to-throw or return-to-sprint bridge with objective measures, unresolved questions, progression/hold criteria, and staff responsibilities; identify medical clearance separately.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Baseball-specific return outcomes and criteria where available; explicit cross-sport extrapolation; agreed clinical/organizational criteria and position demands. No universal threshold can guarantee safety.

competencies.title: Interdisciplinary coordination and care transitions
competencies.description: Align medical, S&C, science, nutrition, baseball, and operations staff around restrictions, priorities, and handoff responsibilities.
competencies.assessment: Run a mock case conference and write a DR-to-US/affiliate transfer handoff with authorized recipient, current restrictions, last exposures, outstanding decisions, receiving-owner confirmation, and reassessment.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Organizational role definitions and authorized handoff/communication standards; supervised multidisciplinary examples. Medical decisions and clearance remain with authorized clinicians.

competencies.title: Player education, trust, and cultural communication
competencies.description: Explain plans in clear player-centered language, check understanding, and invite concerns across language/cultural differences.
competencies.assessment: Give a plain-language teach-back briefing and adapt it for a player’s preferred language using qualified language support where needed; assess understanding without assuming fluency or consent.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Health/coach communication evidence, culturally responsive practice resources, and feedback from qualified speakers and players. Language study does not establish professional medical-language competence.

competencies.title: Recovery, nutrition coordination, and referral
competencies.description: Integrate recovery habits and schedule constraints with the responsibilities of sports medicine, dietitians, and other qualified staff.
competencies.assessment: Make a travel-week recovery plan; identify which questions belong to a dietitian, medical provider, or mental-health professional, and document the referral path.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Sports recovery/sleep/nutrition research and team professional-scope policies. Education and coordination are distinct from individualized medical nutrition therapy or mental-health treatment.

competencies.title: Coach development and departmental standards
competencies.description: Lead through observation, feedback, case review, onboarding, and shared standards while respecting competence and delegated authority.
competencies.assessment: Create a 30-day coach onboarding plan, an observation rubric, and a feedback conversation; distinguish required standards, coach autonomy, and issues to escalate.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Preserved leadership duties, evidence on feedback/learning and team operations, plus real supervised leadership assessment. Course completion cannot substitute for required management experience.

competencies.title: Baseball operations and resource stewardship
competencies.description: Organize facilities, equipment, testing logistics, staff coverage, schedules, and resources at the responsibility level assigned to each role.
competencies.assessment: Build a fictional spring-training equipment/coverage plan with maintenance checks, cost assumptions, travel contingencies, and purchasing approval owners; distinguish affiliate execution from coordinator budget authority.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Organizational SOPs, equipment instructions, realistic cost/coverage data, and the specific role’s delegated authority. Budget ownership is explicit in one club's summary, not assumed for every coach.

competencies.title: Emergency readiness and professional boundaries
competencies.description: Know activation, referral, communication, and assigned first-response responsibilities; maintain required training separately from hub learning.
competencies.assessment: Complete a tabletop emergency scenario with location-specific activation, trained responder assignments, AED access, communication, and receiving-facility handoff; identify actions beyond personal competence.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Current employer emergency action plans and recognized CPR/AED/first-aid/BLS training as applicable; qualified practical assessment. The hub does not issue or renew these credentials.

competencies.title: Accurate records, privacy, and quality improvement
competencies.description: Maintain timely, traceable records with appropriate access; use de-identified review to identify process failures and improve follow-through.
competencies.assessment: Audit a synthetic athlete record for missing dates, units, restrictions, owners, and unauthorized sharing; propose a correction log and one measurable workflow improvement.
competencies.evidenceNeeded: Approved AMS/EMR and access policies, applicable professional requirements, and documentation standards. Medical EMR duties are explicit for one club's medical role; broader governance mappings are curriculum recommendations.

sourceGroups.title: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, fourth edition
sourceGroups.coverage: The supplied CSCS textbook supports the foundation plan for physiology, biomechanics, testing, training, and program design.
sourceGroups.reviewStatus: Selected biomechanics, energetics, training-adaptation, resistance-training, plyometric, speed/agility and aerobic-training passages reviewed for the expanded chapters. Exact PDF and printed-page locators are in the source catalog. This is not a full-book review.

sourceGroups.title: NSCA’s Essentials of Sport Science
sourceGroups.coverage: The supplied CPSS textbook supports measurement, monitoring, applied science, research reasoning, and communication.
sourceGroups.reviewStatus: Selected measurement, statistics, training-design, data-workflow, monitoring and communication passages reviewed. The source catalog and section citations record the reviewed chapter/PDF-page ranges; this is not a full-book review.
sourceGroups.use: Connect measurement and scientific reasoning to baseball tasks, while using baseball research for population-specific claims.

sourceGroups.title: Accessible research and clinical frameworks
sourceGroups.coverage: Current cataloged full texts cover elbow, shoulder, hamstring, measurement, and baseball workload topics; expert practice references are separately labeled.
sourceGroups.reviewStatus: Section-level references accompany the expanded chapters. Source review is editorial; independent clinical expert review remains outstanding.
sourceGroups.use: Support detailed claims, identify study populations and limitations, and distinguish baseball findings from cross-sport extrapolation.

stages.title: Foundations and baseball demands
stages.scope: Functional anatomy, adaptation, energy systems, biomechanics, research interpretation, and the demands of pitchers and position players. Establish what each staff role can decide.
stages.deliverable: A role-specific needs analysis and evidence brief that distinguishes measured demands, assumptions, and unanswered questions.

stages.title: Strength, speed, and programming
stages.scope: Exercise selection and coaching, force and power development, sprinting and deceleration, conditioning, annual plans, in-season microcycles, travel, and changing availability.
stages.deliverable: An annual outline, four-week block, and adaptable game-week plan with exercise rationale and coaching observations.

stages.title: Applied sports science
stages.scope: Test selection, collection protocols, reliability and measurement error, workload records, data cleaning, reproducible analysis, visualization, and staff reporting.
stages.deliverable: A testing SOP, cleaned practice dataset, analysis, and one-page report that supports a named decision without overstating the data.

stages.title: Rehab and return to performance
stages.scope: Shoulder, elbow, and hamstring anatomy and injury mechanisms; operative and nonoperative distinctions; graded loading, testing, throwing, running, and return to role-specific baseball demands.
stages.deliverable: A case-based rehabilitation handoff and return-to-performance plan with permissions, progression questions, monitoring, and remaining uncertainty.

stages.title: Staff handoffs and affiliate operations
stages.scope: Interdisciplinary handoffs, player education, coach development, common standards, affiliate transitions, scheduling, equipment, budgets, emergency readiness, and confidential records.
stages.deliverable: An affiliate operations packet, coach feedback plan, and concise staff communication for a changing player situation.
stages.developmentNote: Baseball handoffs and transitions are practiced in the season case and existing assignments. A broad leadership curriculum belongs to the separate Performance Curriculum project.

stages.title: Integrated professional work samples
stages.scope: Combine the foundation with the relevant role pathway. Defend decisions, revise plans when new evidence arrives, and explain tradeoffs to baseball, medical, and performance staff.
stages.deliverable: A pitcher case, position-player case, and leadership or analysis case, each assessed against a transparent rubric and discussed with an experienced practitioner.
stages.developmentNote: The baseball study paths and cases provide work-sample practice. Observed delivery and independent practitioner feedback remain separate requirements.
